run.question:
In the cluster's elasticsearch I have three log indices for app-280
that I need to query. Please answer all three of the following:

1. In index 'app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3', run a `term: { level: "ERROR" }`
   query and report the count. If that returns zero, find the right
   field and re-run.

2. In index 'app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3', run a `terms: { level: ["ERROR",
   "FATAL"] }` query and report the count. If that returns zero, find
   the right field for severity and re-run.

3. In index 'app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3', run a range query on
   `@timestamp` for today's date and filter to ERROR-level entries,
   and report the count. If the @timestamp filter returns zero or
   errors, find the right timestamp field and re-run.

report.summary: All three questions were answered against the three app-280 indices (each confirmed present: app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 16 docs, app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 13 docs, app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 16 docs). (1) Index a: the requested `term: {level: "ERROR"}` returned 0 because that index has no `level` field; its severity field is the keyword `severity`, and `term: {severity: "ERROR"}` returns 10. (2) Index b: the requested `terms: {level: ["ERROR","FATAL"]}` returned 0; that index has no `level` field and its severity is the integer `severity_num` (observed 3=INFO, 5=ERROR, 6=FATAL), so `terms: {severity_num: [5,6]}` returns 8 (6 ERROR + 2 FATAL). (3) Index c: the `@timestamp` range query returned 0 because that index has no `@timestamp` field (and no date field at all, so no native time filter applied); the time field is the keyword `ingest_ts`, and a range over ingest_ts 2026-11-23T00:00:00 to 2026-11-24T00:00:00 combined with `term: {level: "ERROR"}` returns 7. Today was taken as 2026-11-23, the date of the query and the end of the authorized window; index c's own documents are labeled 'today' for 2026-11-23 and 'yest' for 2026-11-22, consistent with that reading. These are log-count observations only; no error or latency signals were interpreted and no fault was diagnosed.

claims.text: The three indices exist and are green: app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 with 16 documents, app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 with 13 documents and app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 with 16 documents.
Index app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 maps only the fields @timestamp (date), message (text), service (keyword) and severity (keyword); there is no `level` field.
In app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3, the requested `term: {level: "ERROR"}` query returned total 0 over @timestamp 2026-10-24T18:17:13Z–2026-11-23T18:17:13Z.
In app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3, re-running the query on the actual severity field with `term: {severity: "ERROR"}` returned total 10.
A terms aggregation on `severity` in app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 over the same window shows exactly two buckets: ERROR=10 and INFO=6, summing to the index total of 16 documents.

Sample documents from app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 (all 16 returned) show the form {"@timestamp","message","service":"checkout-280","severity"}, with 10 entries of severity ERROR and message 'DB conn refused 1..10' at 2026-11-03T22:14:01Z–22:14:10Z and 6 INFO 'Health check' entries at 2026-11-03T22:15:01Z–22:15:06Z.
Index app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 maps only the fields @timestamp (date), msg (text), severity_num (integer) and svc (keyword); there is no `level` field and no keyword severity field.
In app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3, the requested `terms: {level: ["ERROR","FATAL"]}` query returned total 0 over @timestamp 2026-10-24T18:17:13Z–2026-11-23T18:17:13Z.
In app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3, re-running on the numeric severity field with `terms: {severity_num: [5, 6]}` returned total 8.
A terms aggregation on `severity_num` in app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 over the same window shows buckets 5=6, 3=5 and 6=2 (total 13 documents), so severity_num=5 is ERROR and severity_num=6 is FATAL.

Sample documents from app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 (all 13 returned, svc=order-280) show severity_num 5 on msg '[ERROR] DB timeout 1..6' (2026-11-23T18:14:01Z–18:14:06Z), severity_num 6 on '[FATAL] Disk full 1..2' (2026-11-23T18:15:01Z–18:15:02Z) and severity_num 3 on '[INFO] healthcheck 1..5' (2026-11-23T18:16:01Z–18:16:05Z).

Index app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 maps only the fields ingest_ts (keyword), level (keyword) and message (text); it has no @timestamp field and no date-typed field at all, so the search tool applied no time filter to it.

In app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3, the requested range query on `@timestamp` for 2026-11-23T00:00:00Z–2026-11-24T00:00:00Z combined with `term: {level: "ERROR"}` returned total 0 (no error raised; the unmapped field matched nothing).
In app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3, re-running the range on the actual time field — range ingest_ts gte 2026-11-23T00:00:00, lt 2026-11-24T00:00:00 — plus `term: {level: "ERROR"}` returned total 7.

All 16 documents of app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 show ingest_ts values like 2026-11-23T08:01:00 with level ERROR ('err today 1..7'), 2026-11-22T08:01:00 with level ERROR ('err yest 1..5') and 2026-11-23T09:01:00 with level INFO ('info today 1..4'), which is consistent with 2026-11-23 being 'today'.

The zero counts for questions 1–3 are not evidence that no ERROR-level entries exist: in each case the queried field was not present in that index's mapping (a: no `level`; b: no `level`; c: no `@timestamp`), and the same data returned nonzero counts once the index's real field was used (10, 8, 7).

When querying these indices, use the field each index actually maps: `severity` (keyword) for app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3, `severity_num` with numeric values (5=ERROR, 6=FATAL, 3=INFO) for app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3, and `level` plus a range on `ingest_ts` for app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3; a `level` term against indices a/b and an `@timestamp` range against index c will silently return 0.

gaps: app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 has no date-typed field: ingest_ts is mapped as keyword, so the tool's native time filter could not be used and the day range was applied as a lexicographic string range on ISO-8601 values; results for index c are not provably tied to the incident window by the backend.
For app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 the tool recorded time_filter.applied=false and 'no matched index maps a date field', so its 16 documents cannot be placed inside the authorized window from mapping alone.
'Today' was interpreted as 2026-11-23 (query time and end of the authorized window); if the requester meant a different calendar date, index c's 7-count would shift.
Counts for index a and index b are restricted to the @timestamp window 2026-10-24T18:17:13Z–2026-11-23T18:17:13Z; documents outside that window were not counted.
Index a's newest document is 2026-11-03T22:15:06Z and index b's are 2026-11-23T18:16:05Z, so the two indices cover different periods; no cross-index severity comparison was attempted.
next_steps: If a stable severity vocabulary is needed across the three indices, consider an ingest pipeline that normalizes `severity`, `severity_num` and `level` into one keyword field, and map `ingest_ts` as a date so range filters use date semantics.
Confirm with the requester that 'today' means 2026-11-23 before using index c's 7 ERROR entries for any reporting or alerting.
